findings.description: The new carve-out is stated far more broadly than the vendor's behaviour, and in the permissive direction. "What that mechanism does not reach is a customisation an administrator's policy configures, which stays in force by the vendor's design" reads as: every policy-configured customisation survives the flag. The vendor's own description of `--safe-mode` says the opposite for most of them: "Managed settings policy still applies, including policy-configured hooks, status line, and file-suggestion commands; managed plugins, managed skills, managed CLAUDE.md, and policy-configured MCP servers do not." The true residual is three named things, not "whatever an administrator's policy configures". Three concrete consequences of the sentence as written. (1) It contradicts socrates' own recorded measurement two lines below the identical sentence in docs/gotchas.md:65, which was taken on a machine deploying a managed configuration and reports four external sources without the flag and none with it. (2) If it were true, a policy-configured external tool source would survive the flag, and the empty `allowedMcpServers` allowlist this change deletes did cover exactly that case (docs/gotchas.md:75, "including one from a managed configuration"), so the deletion would be a regression on managed machines rather than the strict improvement line 57 asserts ("that mechanism makes an allowlist for one source of tools pointless"). (3) A reader on a managed machine is told the reviewer may hold policy-configured tool-server tools that neither the flag nor the allowlist stops, which is not what socrates measured or what the vendor documents. The same sentence is at openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:42, AGENTS.md:98 and README.md:140; both AGENTS.md:98 and README.md:140 also keep an absolute heading ("No customisation the machine brings reaches the reviewer", "It does not load your customisations") over a body that now admits a residual. Narrow the carve-out to the policy-configured customisations that actually survive, and say that managed plugins, managed skills, managed memory and policy-configured tool sources do not.

The requirement now contradicts itself about whether a hook contributes a tool, fifteen lines apart. Line 48 (unchanged) justifies the tool-list check with "an external tool server contributes tools, so does a hook, so does a plugin", and the new line 63 justifies the residual with "A policy-configured hook is the case that matters: it contributes no tool, so the session's tool list cannot see it". Both cannot hold, and which one holds decides whether the tool-list check covers hooks at all. The same pair sits inside one bullet at AGENTS.md:98 ("a hook ... [is a way] a tool socrates never asked for ends up in the reviewer's session" followed by "a policy-configured hook contributes no tool, so the tool list cannot see it either"), and in the delta at openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:28 versus 43. Line 63 is the accurate half: a hook runs a command on an event and adds nothing to the session's `tools` array that internal/agent/stream.go:93 reads, so line 48's claim that a hook contributes tools overstates what the one check covers.

The rewritten enumeration of what the vendor's help says the flag disables drops "external tool sources" and adds "workflows, themes and keybindings". The vendor's help lists both: "CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, custom commands and agents, output styles, workflows, custom themes, custom keybindings, status line and file-suggestion commands, LSP servers, and auto memory do not load". Removing the one item that is the entire reason the flag replaced the empty allowlist leaves this file arguing against itself: line 77 still says "`--safe-mode` replaced it because it covers hooks and plugins too", implying it at least matches the allowlist on tool sources, while the list above no longer claims it covers them. It also now contradicts openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/design.md:27, which reports the same help as listing "output styles, and external tool sources". Restore external tool sources to the list.

The change's own documents still carry the unqualified claim the specs, AGENTS.md, README.md and docs/gotchas.md were rewritten to drop: proposal.md:16 "`--safe-mode` disables every customisation the machine brings", proposal.md:25 "One flag replaces the tool-source machinery", and design.md:7 "the vendor already ships a flag that disables every source of the ones socrates did not ask for". These are archived alongside the change and are where a later reader looks for the reasoning, so the record will state the claim without the carve-out that was decided on.

The new scenario and the rewritten requirement were written into the promoted specification at the same time as into the delta, while the change is still open (tasks.md:58 is unticked). internal/promotion reads the promoted spec as the before-state, so with both sides byte-identical the drop gate ticked at tasks.md:56 can report nothing about this change, and the five scenario renames the delta declares (openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:3-16) match no promoted name, one of them being a FROM/TO pair that is identical on both sides (delta:6-7). Coverage is not affected: the new scenario's normalised text is contained in the existing `TestTheReviewerIsGivenToolsThatDoNotWrite` (internal/agent/claude_test.go:151), so `make scenario-coverage` still passes. This repeats round 1's f4, which recorded no response; the state persists and this change adds a promoted scenario to it.

The requirement now names one honest limit of the tool list, a source that connects after the opening event, and stops. The silent one is still unstated and still unhandled: an opening event carrying no `tools` field at all. internal/agent/stream.go:93 assigns whatever the init event held, and internal/agent/claude.go:110-120 returns no unexpected tools for an empty list, so a vendor release that stops emitting `tools` turns "The mechanism SHALL NOT be trusted to have worked" (line 66) into a check that passes on absence of evidence, recording no event for anybody to look at. The unit tests guard the case explicitly (internal/agent/claude_test.go:80-82, "this test would pass on an empty reading"), which is precisely the distinction production code does not make. This repeats round 1's f3, which recorded no response.

risk_rationale: The change is documentation only and touches no executable path, but it rewrites the normative statement of the reviewer's security boundary and states the residual more permissively than either the vendor's documented behaviour or socrates' own recorded measurement.
